hero.lead: I build OCR tools that end manual data entry from receipts and scanned PDFs, plus the web applications and automations that run a small business's daily work. Every delivery comes measured and documented.

items.title: Documents → Excel (OCR)
items.text: Tools that extract company, date, VAT, totals or table data from receipts and scanned PDFs into Excel/JSON. They run on your own computer or server; documents never go to the cloud. Values are cross-checked, and anything uncertain is flagged.

items.title: Web & desktop applications
items.text: Stock and order panels, admin dashboards, price calculators and ordering sites. Role-based access, reports, mobile-friendly UI; deployed on Vercel, Render or Cloudflare. Offline desktop programs as a single .exe (e.g. receivables and installment tracking).

items.title: Automation & APIs
items.text: Handing repetitive work over to scripts: data collection, report and Excel generation. Deploying your tools to your server as an API: HTTPS, API keys, hardening, load testing and documentation.

items.title: Receipt OCR
items.alt: Fields read from a grocery receipt and the resulting JSON
items.problem: Company name, tax ID, date, VAT and totals of hundreds of receipts were typed in by hand for bookkeeping.
items.solution: CPU-only OCR with rule-based field extraction, no cloud or AI services. Rotated and side-by-side receipts are split automatically; VAT and totals are verified against each other. Then deployed to the client's server as an HTTPS API and measured with a load test.
items.result: Drop photos into a folder, get JSON out. A receipt whose amounts don't add up is never written silently; it is flagged for review.
items.note: Source code delivered to the client; contact me for a demo.

items.title: Cari Takip: Receivables & Installment Tracker
items.alt: Cari Takip customer detail screen: installment table, take-payment and WhatsApp reminder buttons
items.problem: Small businesses that sell on credit or in installments keep receivables in a ledger or in Excel, which makes overdue payments hard to spot and chase.
items.solution: A desktop program that works offline: the installment plan is previewed before saving, partial payments are recorded, and a ready-made WhatsApp reminder opens for overdue customers. Amounts are stored as integer kuruş; the rounding remainder goes to the last installment and due dates follow month ends (31 Jan, 28 Feb, 31 Mar).
items.result: Runs as a single .exe and the data stays on the user's computer. The business rules are separate from the UI and verified by 49 automated tests.
items.note: A sample project with no real customer data. Get in touch to discuss a version adapted to your business.

items.title: Scanned PDF → Excel
items.alt: A scanned materials list and the Excel table produced from it
items.problem: Tables in scanned PDFs can't be copied, and Turkish number format (1.250,50) stays as text in most converters, so Excel can't sum it.
items.solution: Pages with a text layer are read directly, scanned pages with OCR; columns are found from whitespace corridors on the page. Web (drag and drop) and desktop interfaces share one core.
items.result: The sample document was converted in 1.2 seconds; numbers are written as real numbers, so formulas work immediately.
items.note: Source code is private; contact me to try it with your own document.

items.title: INTSHOP: Stock & Order Panel
items.alt: INTSHOP store page: product cards with the best dealer prices
items.problem: Admins, dealers and customers needed to work on the same product catalog with different permissions.
items.solution: A three-role application: the admin manages the catalog and price-change requests, dealers set their own stock and prices, customers shop in the store. Stock movements, login logs and charted reports.
items.result: Runs locally with a single Docker Compose command; the admin, dealer and customer roles come with ready demo data. The live demo is offline for now, the code is on GitHub.

items.title: SQL Mastery
items.alt: SQL Mastery lesson page: lesson list and progress bar
items.problem: Beginners lacked a step-by-step SQL resource that needs no installation.
items.solution: A single-page app that opens in the browser: 13 lessons, syntax-highlighted examples, table schemas and progress tracking stored in the browser. No library dependencies.
items.result: 50+ examples, from CREATE TABLE to window functions and stored procedures.

meta.title: Move from WordPress to a custom-coded site · Furkan Çöl
meta.description: I move your WordPress site to a fast, secure, low-maintenance custom-coded site. Content is migrated automatically; URLs and search visibility are preserved.

wp.title: From WordPress to a fast, custom-coded site
wp.lead: Leave theme and plugin bloat behind. I move your site, with the same content, to a setup that loads faster, is more secure and costs less to host. Content is migrated from WordPress automatically and your existing URLs are kept.
wp.cta_note: Send me your site address and I'll tell you what will be moved and how long it will take.

why.title: Loads fast
why.text: Pages are generated ahead of time; no database or plugins run on each visit. Visitors see the content without waiting.

why.title: More secure
why.text: No PHP, plugins or admin login run on the server, so attacks that exploit plugin vulnerabilities disappear.

why.title: Cheap hosting
why.text: Static sites can be hosted for free or at very low cost on services like Cloudflare Pages or GitHub Pages.

why.title: Your design
why.text: You are not bound by a theme's limits. Animation, multiple languages, blog, forms: everything is built for your site.

steps.title: Review
steps.text: I list your pages, blog posts, forms and plugins, and share in writing what stays the same and what changes.

steps.title: Automatic content migration
steps.text: Posts, pages and images are pulled by script through WordPress's own REST API. No manual copying, no lost content.

steps.title: Design and build
steps.text: I build the site on a modern stack (SvelteKit): fast, mobile-friendly, with complete SEO settings.

steps.title: URLs and launch
steps.text: Old URLs are kept as they are or permanently redirected (301), so your search visibility is not hurt. I connect your domain and launch.

wp.case_title: I did the same with my own site
wp.case_text: furkancol.me was moved from an old static generator to SvelteKit: URLs were kept, and two languages, a blog, RSS, light/dark themes and animations were added. It is hosted for free on GitHub Pages and every change is published automatically.

faq.q: Will I be able to edit the content myself?
faq.a: Yes. If you like, I add a free content management panel; you edit posts and pages in a screen similar to WordPress. If you don't need a panel, I handle content updates.
Your URLs are kept or connected to the new ones with 301 redirects, and titles and descriptions move too. That is the standard way to preserve search visibility. Faster pages are a plus.

faq.q: Can an e-commerce (WooCommerce) site be moved too?
faq.a: Sites with payments, carts and accounts are a separate project; I review your needs first and send a separate quote. The quick migration on this page is for brochure, corporate and blog sites.
It depends on the scope. Once I see the number of pages and features, I give an exact timeline and price. Brochure sites usually take a few days.

items.title: ROI Calculator
items.summary: How many months until it pays for itself? A slider-and-chart calculator tuned per industry; the result carries over to the quote form.
items.problem: Businesses that sell equipment could not answer "how fast does it pay back?", and prospects looked at a spreadsheet and walked away.
items.solution: I built a calculator with sliders and a chart that runs on the site. The result pre-fills the quote form. Industry differences live in one config object; a new industry is one added entry. I also fixed usability issues such as a readable chart on mobile and tr-TR thousands separators in inputs.
items.result: A dependency-free (~20 KB) tool embedded with one script tag. Visitors see the payback with their own numbers and leave a request in one click. Requests are listed in the browser and exported as CSV.

items.title: Booking System (hair / beauty salon)
items.summary: Online booking for salons: pick a service, a person and a time; double bookings are blocked at the database level.
items.problem: Hair and beauty salons manage bookings by phone and WhatsApp with a notebook; double bookings and forgotten clients are routine.
items.solution: The client picks a service, a staff member (or "anyone"), a day and a time, then confirms with name and phone. Free slots are computed from working hours, time off, existing bookings and service length. Conflicts are blocked by a PostgreSQL constraint: of two simultaneous requests, one gets "this slot was just taken". Reminders cost nothing: calendar file (.ics), WhatsApp and email links. The salon owner manages the calendar, services and staff from a separate admin panel.
items.result: The client booking flow, admin panel (login, daily/weekly calendar, confirm/cancel, WhatsApp reminders, services/staff/working hours) and the client self-service cancel link are live in the demo. The demo resets every night; demo admin credentials are pre-filled on the login page. Code: github.com/furkancol10/fc-randevu-sistemi

items.title: QR Menu (cafe / restaurant)
items.summary: A sign-up-free TR/EN QR menu for cafes and restaurants: cart-to-WhatsApp ordering with table numbers, plus a category, item and table admin panel.
items.problem: Printed cafe and restaurant menus go stale whenever prices or availability change, and international guests need a second menu. Third-party QR menu platforms add monthly fees and vendor lock-in.
items.solution: Guests scan the table QR code and browse categories, allergens, sold-out flags and prices in Turkish or English on a 360 px mobile menu with no sign-up. Cart items and the verified table label turn into a pre-filled WhatsApp order message in one tap; orders are not stored in the database. From the admin panel, owners manage categories, items, one-tap sold-out status, tables and printable A4 QR table cards, with prices stored as integer kuruş.
items.result: The live demo runs the customer menu, TR/EN switcher, cart-to-WhatsApp flow and admin panel (demo credentials pre-filled on the login page). Demo data resets nightly; image uploads are disabled on the public demo in favor of a built-in gallery. Code: github.com/furkancol10/fc-qr-menu

items.title: Mini CRM: Quote and Job Tracking Panel
items.summary: Customer, job, VAT quote and payment tracking for repair shops and small agencies; customers approve quotes from a tracking link with no login.
items.problem: Repair shops and small agencies keep device intake in notebooks, quotes in spreadsheets and payments in loose notes. After revisions nobody is sure which quote was approved, and customers keep calling for status. Enterprise CRMs are too heavy for a small team.
items.solution: Everything from request to delivery hangs off a single job record: an 8-stage workflow (kanban on desktop, status tabs at 360 px), itemized quotes with 0/10/20% VAT, revision versioning and a print view. Money is computed as integer kuruş; one approved quote per job is enforced by a database index and concurrent status changes by a row lock. Customers open a random link (no personal data shown) to see the job history and approve or reject a quote. Admins see payments and balance; technicians see only their own jobs, enforced server-side.
items.result: No live demo yet. The app runs locally with Docker Compose and ready-made demo data (8 customers, 14 jobs, quotes and payments); the code is on GitHub. Business rules are covered by unit tests, real PostgreSQL integration tests, and Playwright end-to-end tests at 360 px and desktop.

items.title: Competitor Price and Stock Tracker (Telegram alerts)
items.summary: A panel for micro e-commerce sellers that watches competitor product pages for price and stock changes with rules and alerts you on Telegram.
items.problem: In a small shop, opening each competitor page to check price and stock takes time. Noticing late that a rival cut a price or sold out delays your own pricing decisions. Most sellers do not need a complex tool, just a plain screen of tracked products and a heads-up when something changes.
items.solution: Products and competitor page URLs are added from the panel; three rule types exist: price below a target, percentage drop and stock change. Each rule has its own cooldown so the same alert is not repeated back to back. The first reading is the baseline and alerts fire only on later changes. A competitor page that breaks is logged as an error, the run continues and the last valid price is kept. No AI; plain explicit rules. The demo only reads its own built-in mock store, and Telegram alerts show up as records (dry_run); with a bot token configured, the message really goes out.
items.result: No live demo yet. The app runs locally with Docker Compose: change a price in the mock store and watch the alert appear, with a price history chart per competitor in the panel. Panel forms are CSRF-protected, requests are rate-limited per IP, and the limit is 10 products and 20 competitors. 223 automated tests pass on a clean checkout. Code on GitHub.
